name: Microsoft Azure Austria East (Vienna cloud region)
notes: Microsoft Learn lists Austria East (programmatic name austriaeast) with physical location Vienna and availability-zone support; azurespeed lists opening year approx. 2025 with 3 AZs. A-grade for cloud-region existence in Vienna; exact datacenter addresses undisclosed (per methodology, region label is not an address; oe24 2026-07-26 reports Microsoft Austria East sites under construction at Schwechat/Achau/Voesendorf in Lower Austria - see Lower Austria records).

name: Digital Realty Vienna VIE1/VIE2/VIE13
notes: Digital Realty operator page lists three Vienna data centers: VIE1 (Louis-Haefliger-Gasse 10, Bldg 1, 1210, 10,963 sqm), VIE2 (Bldg 2, 20,395 sqm), VIE13 (Siemensstrasse 91, Bldg 1, 18,000 sqm), all 2N+1 cooling, direct VIX access; Digital Realty also publishes EEffG 2025 key figures for VIE01/VIE02 (>=500 kW EEffG reporting confirms sizable IT load). VIE2 also hosts VIX2 IXP location.

name: AtlasEdge Vienna VIE001 (Siemensstrasse 90) / VIE002 planned / VIE003
notes: AtlasEdge official page lists VIE001 in operation at Siemensstrasse 90, Building 38, 1210 Vienna with >900 sqm IT space and alternative carrier routing; data center map reports 2 MVA power (C). VIE002 listed planned by AtlasEdge; VIE003 (Leopoldine-Padaurek-Str. 14, 1210) appears in colocation directories. Acquisition from Siemens Campus Vienna-Floridsdorf with expansion to 10 MW reported (B).

name: A1 Telekom Next Generation Data Center (NGDC) / Exoscale AT-VIE-1 Arsenal & AT-VIE-2
notes: Exoscale operator page: AT-VIE-1 hosted by A1 Telekom in Arsenal (Objekt 24, Vienna, former military building), AT-VIE-2 in A1 Next Generation Data Center (NGDC), Vienna; N+1 redundancy, ISO 27001. A1 Digital states Vienna DC is one of 14 A1 datacenters in Austria with coverage in every provincial capital (A for the coverage statement; local facility details in other states need separate proof).

name: BRZ Bundesrechenzentrum (federal datacenter)
notes: BRZ official pages: federal IT service provider based at Hintere Zollamtsstrasse 4, 1030 Vienna, operating one of Austria's largest datacenter environments for public administration (federal government datacenter, not commercial colo).

name: VIX Vienna Internet Exchange VIX1-VIX3 / NTT Vienna-1
developer: VIX (Vienna Internet eXchange) / NTT Global Data Centers EMEA
notes: VIX official locations page: VIX1 at University of Vienna ZID (Universitaetsstrasse 7, 1010), VIX2 at Digital Realty Austria (Louis-Haefliger-Gasse 10, 1210), VIX3 at NTT Global Data Centers EMEA AT GmbH (Computerstrasse 4, 1100 Vienna) - the latter confirms an NTT Vienna-1 datacenter facility in the south of the city. IXP interconnection evidence (A for locations; facility detail of NTT per its own global page).

name: Digital Realty/Interxion Vienna expansion land (up to 40 MW)
notes: DCD reports Interxion/Digital Realty land acquisition near the Vienna campus for a data center with up to 40 MW IT capacity (B-grade expansion report; build status to be verified against operator/permit sources before counting as built capacity).

name: CloudHQ Leopoldsdorf mega data center
notes: oe24 (2026-07-26): US group CloudHQ plans a data center south of the Vienna city border in Leopoldsdorf from 2027; three buildings with ~200 MW connection capacity in final stage, 70 MW in first stage (per CloudHQ manager Andreas Graf-Matzner); closed-loop water cooling, waste-heat re-use considered, EUR 9m community package. Permit process starts with construction start 2027. Status announced/planned; B-grade press until municipal permit or operator confirmation.

name: Microsoft Austria East data centers (Schwechat, Achau, Voesendorf)
notes: oe24 (2026-07-26) reports large Microsoft Cloud Region Austria data centers being built around Vienna in Schwechat (Bezirk Bruck an der Leitha), Achau and Voesendorf (Bezirk Moedling), citing Microsoft's website. B-grade press for municipality-level sites of the Azure Austria East region; addresses/sites not yet confirmed by Microsoft official pages (methodology: do not assign Azure facilities to Lower Austria without a source naming the municipality - this press source does name them).

name: Niederoesterreich Rechenzentren-Strategie (state datacenter strategy/zoning program)
notes: Official state press release (2026-04-16): Lower Austria is first Bundesland with a dedicated datacenter strategy - new zoning category 'Bauland-Sondergebiet-Rechenzentrum', size categories (<=0.5 ha, <=3 ha, >3 ha requiring state ordinance), priority grid access for public/critical infrastructure; ~3,400 MW of datacenter project inquiries pending (double the state's electricity consumption). Official planning/policy evidence (lead source, not a facility itself); municipalities must be verified individually.

name: Google Kronstorf data center
notes: Google announced ground-breaking 2026-04-23 for its first Austrian data center in Kronstorf, Upper Austria (A); ~100 direct jobs, heat-recovery ready; DCD reports 70 ha site / 42,000 sqm project scope (B); NÖ state press release cites ~150 MW Anschlussleistung for the Google facility (A-grade official quote), also seen in trade coverage (C). Not to be equated with a live GCP region.

name: LINZ AG TELEKOM IT- und Data Center Linz 1 / Linz 2
notes: LINZ AG TELEKOM operator/news pages: Data Center Linz 1 at Oberfeldstrasse 4, 4021 Linz (600 sqm server area, 204 racks, ~9,000 servers on two levels per itwelt B) and second IT- und Data Center Linz 2 opened spring 2025 in Linz. Municipal-utility owned colocation/hosting for customers plus in-house systems.

name: eworx Datacenter Linz & Perg
notes: eworx operator page: datacenter in Upper Austria offering hosting, housing and cloud services at locations in Linz and Perg (Technologiepark 17, 4320 Perg per company profile). Operator-stated facilities (A/B).

name: Data Center Perg (Technologiezentrum Perg)
notes: Technologiezentrum Perg markets 'Data Center Perg', a modern data/server center offering professional server floor space and services (B/A for its own facility/service statement).

name: Fragmentix Lend AI Data Center (LendAIDC)
notes: Local/regional press (2025-09-27): Fragmentix builds AI/high-security data center in Lend, Salzburg in a repurposed industrial hall; planned total power 25 MW from local existing hydro plants; first test servers already running for Austrian authorities; Dell hardware with full Austrian control; EU-RESTRICTED-classified data capability. B-grade press; operator/permit/grid confirmation still recommended (methodology: treat as lead until primary confirmation).

name: Magenta Rechenzentrum Graz
notes: Magenta newsroom (2022-05-23): new Magenta data center opened in Graz with double-digit million euro investment, built/operated by COOLtec Systems (groundbreaking spring 2021); ORF (B) and derStandard (B) confirm opening and technical details. Operational.

name: Nexspace Graz data center (Alte Poststrasse)
notes: Nexspace operator page markets Graz data center colocation (A/B); directory lists Alte Poststrasse 376 (C corroboration; EDIS lists T-Systems/Nexspace building at Alte Poststrasse 365, 8055 Graz). COOLtec-origin facility per Magenta/project-partner context.

name: Citycom Datacenter Graz
notes: Citycom Graz network/datacenter lead via PeeringDB facility 1119 and operator site (C/B). Interconnection evidence only; facility details, ownership and status require operator-page or permit confirmation before counting as high-confidence facility inventory.

name: Datencenter 3 - Hall in Tirol
notes: Aggregator listing only: Datencenter 3 - Hall in Tirol, Augasse 6, Hall in Tirol 6060. No operator page, permit or grid evidence found. C-grade seed; A1's provincial-capital coverage makes Innsbruck a search lead but no named A1 facility was verified in this pass. Tyrol otherwise has no confirmed datacenter project.

name: Datacenter Feldkirch (Stadtwerke Feldkirch)
notes: Stadtwerke Feldkirch official page: modern Datacenter Feldkirch offering colocation/server housing (shared and private 19-inch racks), 250 sqm white space, 69 racks, 2N redundant power/cooling circuits, 100% green power, 99.99% availability guarantee, meet-me room. Municipal-utility colocation facility in the Vierlaendereck (A-grade operator page; new verified facility beyond methodology seed list). Historical VRZ Dornbirn references remain C/historical and are not counted.

name: Klagenfurt 'Cyber-City' / Lakeside Quartiere data center plan
developer: Stadt Klagenfurt / Lakeside Science & Technology Park (to be confirmed)
notes: Kleine Zeitung (2023-02-18): west Klagenfurt tech park on former Rohrer grounds ('Lakeside Quartiere') to include a data center and cooling-technology center as core infrastructure; tenant list open. B-grade press for the planning intent; no operator, permit or grid evidence yet - planned/lead only. Lakeside Science & Technology Park itself is an ICT cluster, not a datacenter per se.

name: Nickelsdorf large data center (up to 50 ha)
notes: ORF Burgenland (2026-08-03): speculation/talks about a datacenter up to 50 ha near Nickelsdorf on land owned by the Burgenland economic agency; Landesholding spokesman says talks with various interested parties are ongoing but no imminent construction; Netz Burgenland confirms multiple grid-connection inquiries but declines details for regulatory reasons; mayor informed mid-August 2026. U for project status (rumor/talks only, no operator or authority confirmation); B only for the existence of public speculation.

name: Digital Burgenland / EBRZ (Eisenstadt)
developer: Digital Burgenland GmbH (formerly Erstes Burgenlaendisches Rechenzentrum)
notes: Digital Burgenland official page: founded 1970 as Erstes Burgenlaendisches Rechenzentrum GmbH; ASP (application service provider) with printing/letter-shop center, based at Kasernenstrasse 9, 7000 Eisenstadt; part of Landesholding Burgenland group. Public-sector IT provider with datacenter operations (B/A for self-description); specific colocation facility details require operator-page confirmation before classing as public colocation.

name: A1 regional datacenter coverage (Eisenstadt lead)
notes: A1 Digital states A1 offers datacenter space in every Austrian provincial capital (14 A1 datacenters nationwide). For Burgenland (Eisenstadt) this is a coverage lead only; no exact A1 facility address was verified in this pass (U/C until operator source names the site). Same logic applies to provincial-capital leads in Tyrol (Innsbruck), Vorarlberg (Bregenz), Carinthia (Klagenfurt), Lower Austria (St. Poelten), Salzburg and Styria (Graz).

name: A1 Salzburg regional datacenter (lead)
notes: A1 provincial-capital coverage makes Salzburg city a datacenter lead, but no exact address or public colo availability was verified from reviewed sources (C lead). No hyperscale or major state-level DC project confirmed for Salzburg beyond the Fragmentix LendAIDC.

name: A1 Innsbruck regional datacenter (lead)
notes: A1 provincial-capital coverage makes Innsbruck a search lead, but no exact current A1 facility address was verified (C lead; methodology: do not assert a named facility without operator/permit source). Magenta Innsbruck colocation appears only in third-party listings (C).

name: A1 Bregenz regional datacenter (lead) / historical VRZ Dornbirn
developer: A1 Telekom Austria (lead); historical Vorarlberger Rechenzentrum (not current)
notes: A1 provincial-capital coverage makes Bregenz a lead (C, no address verified). Historical 'Vorarlberger Rechenzentrum'/Dornbirn references are not current facility evidence (C historical). Datacenter Feldkirch (see above) is the only verified current colocation facility in Vorarlberg in this pass.

name: A1 Klagenfurt regional datacenter (lead)
notes: A1 provincial-capital coverage makes Klagenfurt a datacenter lead (C, no address verified). Lakeside Science & Technology Park is an ICT cluster, not a datacenter proof by itself; the Cyber-City plan (above) is the only named Carinthian DC project lead.

name: A1 St. Poelten regional datacenter (lead)
notes: A1 provincial-capital coverage makes St. Poelten a likely A1 regional facility lead, but no address should be asserted from the A1 Digital source alone (C lead). Main Lower Austria projects in this pass: CloudHQ Leopoldsdorf and Microsoft Austria East sites at Schwechat/Achau/Voesendorf.

name: A1 Graz regional datacenter (lead)
notes: A1 provincial-capital coverage makes Graz a datacenter lead independent of Magenta/Nexspace (C, no address verified). Styria's confirmed facilities in this pass: Magenta Graz, Nexspace Graz, Citycom lead.

name: AWS/OCI Austria region absence (negative check)
notes: Negative control per methodology: AWS global infrastructure pages list no Austrian region/AZ and Oracle OCI region docs list no Austrian public cloud region (A-grade absence). Equinix has no Austrian IBX in its official EMEA footprint; beware Vienna, VA false positives. Any AWS/OCI Austria facility claim should be treated as unsupported unless a provider source appears.
